host.label: IP address or host name of the Violet

username.label: User name
username.tooltip: Login of the Violet web interface (usually not needed for reading only)

allow_switching.label: Allow switching (ON / OFF / AUTO)
allow_switching.tooltip: Creates a data point "schalten" for each function. Dosing, cover and Violet settings are deliberately not switchable.

switch_duration.label: Duration for manual ON/OFF (minutes)
switch_duration.tooltip: 0 = permanently, until switched back to AUTO

switchNote.text: User name and password of the Violet are usually required for switching. Not switchable: dosing, cover, settings.

web_enabled.label: Provide pool display
web_enabled.tooltip: Built-in web server: http://<ioBroker-IP>:<port>/ – use only in your home network, do not expose to the internet

webNote.text: Address: http://<ioBroker-IP>:<port>/ – switches in the pool display only if "Allow switching" is enabled. Use only in your home network.

intro.text: What do you use on your Violet? Only checked areas are created as data points.

water_freeze.label: Freeze water values while the pump is off
water_freeze.tooltip: Electrodes only measure correctly with flow. With the pump off the last valid values are kept (marked with * in the pool display, no red marking).

use_pump_rpm.label: Pump with speed levels
use_pump_rpm.tooltip: Only for speed-controlled pumps with levels 0–3

h2.text: Dosing – which channels are in operation?

eloinfo.text: The Violet does not report operating hours of the cell. The adapter adds up the runtime itself; the data point "zelle_gewechselt" resets the counter (only in ioBroker).

elo_output.label: Cell output – g chlorine per hour
elo_output.tooltip: See type plate or data sheet; empty = no grams per day

elo_lifetime.label: Cell lifetime – hours
elo_lifetime.tooltip: Usually 3000–6000 h according to the manufacturer

elo_start_hours.label: Hours already run (start value)
elo_start_hours.tooltip: For a cell that has already been running. Replaces the counter when changed.

use_temp.label: Temperature sensors
use_temp.tooltip: Sensors that are not connected are omitted automatically; names in the tab "Temperatures"

use_analog.label: Analog / pulse inputs
use_analog.tooltip: e.g. filter pressure, humidity, probe flow – names and units in the tab "Analog"

use_details.label: Switching times and runtimes
use_details.tooltip: Creates 3 additional data points per function

use_messages.label: Violet messages (warnings, alarms, reminders)
use_messages.tooltip: Data point meldungen.aktiv and notice in the pool display; acknowledging only affects ioBroker

ht.text: Sensors 1–6 are permanently assigned in the Violet and are named automatically as there (own name optional). From sensor 7 freely nameable. The current value is shown next to each field.

temp1_pump_only.label: Water temperature (sensor 1) is only realistic while the pump runs
temp1_pump_only.tooltip: Sensor in the pump piping: with the pump off the value is frozen (data point temperatur.sensor1_pool), marked with * in the pool display

ha.text: The Violet has fixed inputs (see labels). Only inputs with a name are created as data points; empty unit = suggestion in grey. The live value helps with the assignment.

hpump.text: Enter the delivery rate of the pump in m³/h. The adapter then calculates the water volume circulated today from the runtimes of the Violet (data point pumpe.umwaelzung_heute, in the pool display behind the runtime). If the absorber or heating reduces the flow, enter the lower value there – empty = same as alone. If both run at the same time, the lower value applies.

hheatinfo.text: Calculates the heat output in kW and the heat energy of today in kWh: (return − water temperature sensor 1) × flow of the running pump level × 1.163. Uses the delivery rates entered above.

heat_return_position.label: Position of the heating return sensor
heat_return_position.tooltip: If both run at the same time: heating = total − absorber

heater_type.label: Type of heating
heater_type.tooltip: Name of the heating in the pool display

hrange.text: Optimal ranges – values outside are shown in red (empty = no check)

hrows.text: Temperature rows of the pool display

hrowsinfo.text: Per row a main sensor and a small second line. The lists show name and current value (instance must be running). All rows empty = automatic.

hrinfo.text: Give the relays a name, e.g. "Garden light". Named relays appear with their name in ioBroker and in the relay view of the pool display.

hrvinfo.text: For devices not connected to the Violet (e.g. garden light via another adapter): name + ioBroker data point (true/false). Only ON/OFF, no automatic. Switchable in the pool display if "Allow switching" is enabled.
